1.web: “Do you know the time when the mountain goats give birth? Do you watch when the doe bears fawns?
1.asv: Knowest thou the time when the wild goats of the rock bring forth? Or canst thou mark when the hinds do calve?

2.web: Can you number the months that they fulfill? Or do you know the time when they give birth?
2.asv: Canst thou number the months that they fulfil? Or knowest thou the time when they bring forth?

3.web: They bow themselves, they bear their young. They end their labor pains.
3.asv: They bow themselves, they bring forth their young, They cast out their pains.

4.web: Their young ones become strong. They grow up in the open field. They go out, and don’t return again.
4.asv: Their young ones become strong, they grow up in the open field; They go forth, and return not again.

5.web: “Who has set the wild donkey free? Or who has loosened the bonds of the swift donkey,
5.asv: Who hath sent out the wild ass free? Or who hath loosed the bonds of the swift ass,

6.web: Whose home I have made the wilderness, and the salt land his dwelling place?
6.asv: Whose home I have made the wilderness, And the salt land his dwelling-place?

7.web: He scorns the tumult of the city, neither does he hear the shouting of the driver.
7.asv: He scorneth the tumult of the city, Neither heareth he the shoutings of the driver.

8.web: The range of the mountains is his pasture, He searches after every green thing.
8.asv: The range of the mountains is his pasture, And he searcheth after every green thing.

9.web: “Will the wild ox be content to serve you? Or will he stay by your feeding trough?
9.asv: Will the wild-ox be content to serve thee? Or will he abide by thy crib?

10.web: Can you hold the wild ox in the furrow with his harness? Or will he till the valleys after you?
10.asv: Canst thou bind the wild-ox with his band in the furrow? Or will he harrow the valleys after thee?

11.web: Will you trust him, because his strength is great? Or will you leave to him your labor?
11.asv: Wilt thou trust him, because his strength is great? Or wilt thou leave to him thy labor?

12.web: Will you confide in him, that he will bring home your seed, and gather the grain of your threshing floor?
12.asv: Wilt thou confide in him, that he will bring home thy seed, And gatherthe grainof thy threshing-floor?

13.web: “The wings of the ostrich wave proudly; but are they the feathers and plumage of love?
13.asv: The wings of the ostrich wave proudly; But are they the pinions and plumage of love?

14.web: For she leaves her eggs on the earth, warms them in the dust,
14.asv: For she leaveth her eggs on the earth, And warmeth them in the dust,

15.web: and forgets that the foot may crush them, or that the wild animal may trample them.
15.asv: And forgetteth that the foot may crush them, Or that the wild beast may trample them.

16.web: She deals harshly with her young ones, as if they were not hers. Though her labor is in vain, she is without fear,
16.asv: She dealeth hardly with her young ones, as if they were not hers: Though her labor be in vain, she is without fear;

17.web: because God has deprived her of wisdom, neither has he imparted to her understanding.
17.asv: Because God hath deprived her of wisdom, Neither hath he imparted to her understanding.

18.web: When she lifts up herself on high, she scorns the horse and his rider.
18.asv: What time she lifteth up herself on high, She scorneth the horse and his rider.

19.web: “Have you given the horse might? Have you clothed his neck with a quivering mane?
19.asv: Hast thou given the horsehismight? Hast thou clothed his neck with the quivering mane?

20.web: Have you made him to leap as a locust? The glory of his snorting is awesome.
20.asv: Hast thou made him to leap as a locust? The glory of his snorting is terrible.

21.web: He paws in the valley, and rejoices in his strength. He goes out to meet the armed men.
21.asv: He paweth in the valley, and rejoiceth in his strength: He goeth out to meet the armed men.

22.web: He mocks at fear, and is not dismayed, neither does he turn back from the sword.
22.asv: He mocketh at fear, and is not dismayed; Neither turneth he back from the sword.

23.web: The quiver rattles against him, the flashing spear and the javelin.
23.asv: The quiver rattleth against him, The flashing spear and the javelin.

24.web: He eats up the ground with fierceness and rage, neither does he stand still at the sound of the trumpet.
24.asv: He swalloweth the ground with fierceness and rage; Neither believeth he that it is the voice of the trumpet.

25.web: As often as the trumpet sounds he snorts, ‘Aha!’ He smells the battle afar off, the thunder of the captains, and the shouting.
25.asv: As oft as the trumpetsoundethhe saith, Aha! And he smelleth the battle afar off, The thunder of the captains, and the shouting.

26.web: “Is it by your wisdom that the hawk soars, and stretches her wings toward the south?
26.asv: Is it by thy wisdom that the hawk soareth, And stretcheth her wings toward the south?

27.web: Is it at your command that the eagle mounts up, and makes his nest on high?
27.asv: Is it at thy command that the eagle mounteth up, And maketh her nest on high?

28.web: On the cliff he dwells, and makes his home, on the point of the cliff, and the stronghold.
28.asv: On the cliff she dwelleth, and maketh her home, Upon the point of the cliff, and the stronghold.

29.web: From there he spies out the prey. His eyes see it afar off.
29.asv: From thence she spieth out the prey; Her eyes behold it afar off.

30.web: His young ones also suck up blood. Where the slain are, there he is.”
30.asv: Her young ones also suck up blood: And where the slain are, there is she.
